content.title: About
content.content: Butternut is a variety of winter squash with a tan skin and sweet, creamy flesh. Raw butternut is rich in vitamins, minerals, and antioxidants, offering a slightly nutty flavor and crisp texture. It is used in salads, marinades, and as an ingredient in fresh juices.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Butternut originated in North America, where it was cultivated by Native Americans long before European settlement.
Unlike many other squashes, butternut can be stored for up to six months under proper conditions.
Its beta‑carotene content is 2‑3 times higher than that of carrots.
Raw butternut is popular in Japanese cuisine for dishes like “tenkasu” and in Korean salads.
The skin is edible and adds extra dietary fiber.

items.title: Rich source of vitamin A
items.content: Beta‑carotene, which converts to vitamin A, supports vision, immunity, and skin health.

items.title: High in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C boosts antioxidant protection and aids iron absorption.

items.title: Potassium and magnesium
items.content: These minerals help regulate blood pressure and support muscle function.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber improves digestion, promotes satiety, and supports gut microbiota.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Flavonoids and carotenoids protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience an allergic reaction to squash.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Raw butternut contains oxalates, which can contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible individuals.

items.title: Digestive discomfort
items.content: Large amounts of raw squash may cause gas and stomach upset.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Slice the butternut thinly and add to salads, use in marinades, blend into fresh juices, or grate into vegetable stir‑fries. Before eating, wash thoroughly and, if desired, peel the skin.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store butternut in a cool, dry place at 0‑10 °C. For long‑term storage, keep it in the refrigerator in a ventilated bag. Avoid storing near ethylene‑producing fruits.
